text.en: Have you ever seen a banyan tree with hanging roots, a bird diving into water or a spider weaving its web? The students and their teacher go on a nature trail to Pachmarhi in Madhya Pradesh, with Abha Didi, a nature scientist, as their guide. They watch animals at a pond, listen to birds, meet an insect and collect leaves. At the end they play the web of life game and discover that every living thing in nature is connected to the others.

Abha Didi welcomed the students at the forest entrance and said they must make sure not to harm the plants and animals. Be careful in a new place and do not tease animals or feed them. Do not damage trees and flowers, and do not throw garbage in the forest. Do not bring pets, weapons or polythene bags, and do not damage public utilities. These rules matter because animals can be harmed by food we give or by plastic, and because forests are the homes of the animals.
Animals on land and birds in the sky have different features that help them live. An elephant has a long trunk to take food and water, and a sparrow has a short strong beak to crack seeds. The Indian Giant Squirrel is a big, red squirrel found in Pachmarhi and some other places. The Spectacled Monkey is the state animal of Tripura, and the white patches around its eyes look like spectacles. At a pond the students saw a gaur, which looks like a buffalo but is stronger and has shorter horns. They also saw footprints in the mud, and by looking at them you can guess which animals came to drink water.
A bird with a long tail and a large curved beak was a hornbill, named for the horn-like headgear on its forehead. Peacocks are colourful, and owls have sharp eyesight to see at night. Different birds have different beaks and claws, and these help them eat and do other things. An eagle has a sharp curved beak and sharp claws to catch its prey, and a sunbird has a long beak to drink nectar from flowers. So by looking at a bird's beak and claws we can guess what it eats. To make a bird diary, stand near a tree, listen to the sounds, focus on one bird and note its colours, beak shape and what it does.
Animals that live in and around water have special features to survive. Fish have fins to swim, crabs walk, frogs jump and turtles swim. The gharial is a type of crocodile with a long, narrow, pointed snout to catch fish. Turtles have strong shells to keep them safe and webbed feet to swim easily. Frogs can live both on land and in water.
A grasshopper hopped out of the grass, and Arya said it is an insect. An insect has three pairs of legs, which means six legs, and one pair of antennae to sense its surroundings. Some insects have two pairs of wings, like flies and grasshoppers. In the forest you can find ants, beetles, bees, flies, praying mantises and butterflies. The forest has a wonderful diversity of animals, each with its own special features.
The students collected leaves and noticed that they differ in colour, shape and feel, which we call texture. Leaves also have lines on them called veins. You can make a leaf autograph by placing a leaf vein side up under a plain paper and rubbing a crayon over it, and the shape and pattern appear. Each leaf has its own pattern, so a leaf can help us name the plant or tree it came from.
In the web of life game each player gets a card with a plant, an animal or a natural element like the Sun or a river. One player holds a ball of yarn, thinks of a connection, for example a tree gives food to a bird, and passes the yarn to that player while still holding the thread. The web keeps growing as more connections are made. If one part is removed, like the deer that a tiger needs, or plants that animals need, the web weakens and may collapse. This shows that everything in nature is connected, and we must care for every living thing.

problem.en: How can you guess what a bird eats?

text.en: Look at its beak and claws.

why.en: They are shaped for the bird's food.

text.en: A short strong beak like a sparrow's cracks seeds.

why.en: A strong short beak can break hard grains.

text.en: A sharp curved beak and claws like an eagle's catch prey, and a long thin beak like a sunbird's drinks nectar.

problem.en: Is a spider an insect? Check with the insect rule.

text.en: An insect has three pairs of legs, which is six legs.

why.en: This is the rule from the chapter.

text.en: A spider has eight legs.
So a spider is not an insect, even though it is a tiny animal.

why.en: It does not match the rule.

prompt.en: Explain the web of life game and what it teaches us about nature.

requiredIdeas.en: Each player is a plant, an animal or part of nature
Yarn joins connected players, for example tree and bird
Removing one part weakens or breaks the web
Everything in nature is connected, so care for all

commonMisconceptions.en: Tigers do not need other animals or plants
Plants are not part of the web

points.en: Follow forest rules: do not feed or tease animals, litter or damage plants.
Beaks and claws tell us what a bird eats.
Insects have three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae.
Leaves have different colours, shapes, textures and veins.
All living things are connected like a web, so protecting one protects all.
